## Details
### **SW-REQ-SCH-001** — Application Registration With Fixed Period

- **Description:** The SCH library shall register applications with a fixed period at startup.
- **Rationale:** PM-mandated static TDM model: every application has a compile-time period set during initialization.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-010
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SCH-002** — Static Schedule After Initialization

- **Description:** The SCH library shall reject application registration after scheduler initialization completes.
- **Rationale:** PM decision SW-REQ-SYS-010: schedule is fixed at compile time; no dynamic registration permitted after init.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-010
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SCH-003** — Periodic Application Invocation

- **Description:** The SCH library shall invoke each registered application at its registered period.
- **Rationale:** Core TDM behavior: apps run on their fixed cadence so sensor and nav rates are met deterministically.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-010
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SCH-004** — Period Range Covers FSW Application Rates

- **Description:** The SCH library shall support application periods spanning at least 5 milliseconds to 500 milliseconds.
- **Rationale:** Constrains the static schedule (SW-REQ-SYS-010) to cover all FT1 app rates: IMU 200 Hz (SYS-005), altimeter 20 Hz (SYS-008), GPS 5 Hz (SYS-009), nav 100 Hz (SYS-012), and telemetry 2 Hz (SYS-019).
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-010
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SCH-005** — Deterministic Invocation Order

- **Description:** The SCH library shall invoke applications in a deterministic order on every scheduler cycle.
- **Rationale:** PM-required determinism (SW-REQ-SYS-044) so Trick simulation and flight runs are repeatable.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-044
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SCH-006** — Scheduler Continues After Application Failure

- **Description:** The SCH library shall continue invoking other registered applications when one application returns a failure status.
- **Rationale:** PM decision: app failures must not halt the scheduler; other apps continue running per SW-REQ-SYS-062.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-062
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SCH-007** — Application Lifecycle Start Invocation

- **Description:** The SCH library shall invoke each registered application's start hook once before its first periodic invocation.
- **Rationale:** Required so apps initialize internal state once before periodic processing begins per LibJuno app lifecycle.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-010
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SCH-008** — POSIX and Pico2 Functional Equivalence

- **Description:** The SCH library shall produce equivalent application invocation sequences on POSIX and Pico2 builds.
- **Rationale:** PM-required POSIX/Pico2 equivalence (SW-REQ-SYS-043) so Trick simulation exercises identical scheduling paths.
- **Verification Method:** Test
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-043
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SCH-009** — Scheduler Capacity Bounded At Compile Time

- **Description:** The SCH library shall enforce a compile-time bound on the number of registered applications.
- **Rationale:** PM constraint: no dynamic memory allocation; capacity must be a compile-time constant per SW-REQ-SYS-050.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-010
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1

### **SW-REQ-SCH-010** — Caller-Owned Scheduler Storage

- **Description:** The SCH library shall use only caller-provided storage and shall not allocate memory dynamically.
- **Rationale:** PM NFR (SW-REQ-SYS-050): no dynamic allocation after boot; all storage caller-owned per LibJuno pattern.
- **Verification Method:** Inspection
- **Status:** Draft
- **Parent:** SW-REQ-SYS-050
- **Children:** None
- **Tags:** FT1
